stemMarkdown: A man travels from A to B at 30 km/h and returns along the same road at 40 km/h. What is his average speed (in km/h) for the whole journey? (Round to 4 decimal places.)
solutionMarkdown: Average speed is total distance over total time, not the average of the two speeds. Taking the one-way distance as $d$: time $= \dfrac{d}{30} + \dfrac{d}{40}$, so average speed $= \dfrac{2d}{d/30 + d/40} = \dfrac{2 \times 30 \times 40}{30 + 40} = 34.2857$.
altSolutionMarkdown: For equal distances the answer is the harmonic mean. The plain average $\dfrac{30 + 40}{2} = 35.0$ is the classic wrong answer, and it is always too high.
